def: Any word that leaves your thumbs bearing no resemblance to what your brain sent. The entire genre of garbled texting, named in a 12:47 a.m. moment of accidental genius.
ex: what should we call the dictionary

def: The mysterious Scandinavian man who appears in your chat when you fall asleep mid-conversation. Nobody knows Sven. Sven knows everybody. He has never once explained himself.
French for “the end,” typed by someone whose brain has already left the conversation. A dramatic curtain call — usually delivered 40 minutes before the texter sends six more messages.
meant: I'm done talking (narrator: he was not)
ex: you said fin an hour ago

def: The family-friendly stand-in your phone swaps in at the worst possible moment, transforming raw fury into a waterfowl situation. Nobody has ever been ducking anything on purpose.
ex: I ducking told you the meeting moved
sir this is the group chat with your boss in it

def: What “definitely” becomes after midnight. Accidentally turns every agreement into a small act of rebellion: “I will defiantly be there” sounds like you're attending under protest.
ex: ill defiantly help you move saturday
you don't have to sound so brave about it

def: One letter and a period: the most dangerous message in the English language. Contains more hostility per character than any text ever sent. Entire relationships have been ended by “k.” and its colder sibling, “k”
ex: we need to talk about the dishes

def: A keyboard smash expressing an emotion too large for language — joy, rage, secondhand embarrassment, or seeing your crush type your name. The home row is the first casualty of feeling things.
meant: I have no words, so here are all of them at once

def: “On the way.” Translation: still on the couch, one shoe located, reconsidering the entire plan. A legally binding promise that means absolutely nothing.
ex: you sent that from your couch last time

def: A unit of time invented by texters, equal to anywhere between 20 and 90 actual minutes. The “5” is decorative. The “away” is aspirational.
meant: geography has not yet been consulted

def: A message composed entirely by a back pocket, consisting of symbols, half-words, and one accidental emoji. Often more honest than anything the owner has typed on purpose.
ex: it says more than i do

def: Texting while face-down and technically unconscious, producing long strings of punctuation, tildes, and yen symbols. The forehead has a vocabulary of roughly nine characters and unlimited confidence.
ex: that was your forehead wasn't it

def: “Good night,” compressed to its bare minimum by someone too tired for vowels. Frequently sent at 4 p.m. Frequently followed by three more hours of texting.
ex: gn stands for 'good, no?' in my heart

def: A declared exit from the conversation, delivered with the finality of a mic drop. The texter will return in approximately three minutes with a screenshot and “ok but look at this.”
meant: I am leaving (terms and conditions apply)

def: “The,” after a long day. The internet's founding typo, still appearing in group chats nightly like it pays rent there.
ex: teh group chat has seen things

def: “You,” typed by a thumb with ambitions bigger than its aim. Impossible to read without hearing it in a tiny, wrong voice.
ex: yuo dont know how to type jungxt

def: The typing “…” that appears, pulses with promise, and vanishes without a message. Somewhere, a masterpiece was written, judged, and deleted. We will never know its name.
meant: a thought that didn't survive review
ex: what were you typing for 4 minutes

def: A read receipt timestamped deep in the night, followed by total silence. Not a rejection — a monument. The message was seen, considered, and filed under “problems for tomorrow.”
meant: I saw it. I chose peace.
ex: my eyes were awake. i was not

def: A 3 a.m. snack so questionable it glows in the dark and doubles as a nightlight. Side effects include hunger, regret, and gases the UN has been notified about.
meant: leftover pizza, reheated with no supervision
ex: glows. no flashlight needed for midnight snacks

def: Weapons-grade flatulence produced by radioactive snack choices. Certified by no authority. Felt by everyone in the building.
Deployed exclusively by people who know exactly who dis. A diplomatic fiction that buys the sender 30 seconds to remember why they stopped replying in the first place.
meant: I know who this is. I am stalling.
ex: your lock screen is a photo of us

def: “Laughing out loud,” typed with a completely straight face since 2009. Now functions purely as punctuation — a softener, a filler, a tiny white flag at the end of a risky sentence.
meant: I acknowledge your message and feel nothing

def: “Owned,” after the O key lost a fight. An ancient gaming-era typo so beloved it got promoted to a real word — proof that a jungxt, repeated enough, becomes law.

pron: the sound of a phone on a face
def: The final transmission of a dying conversation: a thumb resting on the Z key as its owner crosses into sleep. Each additional z is one more second of plausible deniability.
meant: I have fallen asleep on the keyboard
ex: and thats why i think the meeting should be— zzzzzzzzz

def: The unofficial email signature of the sleep-texter. Explains everything: the tildes, the yen symbols, the mysterious man named Sven. No apology included, because the sender is asleep.
